title: 6061-T651 Plate: How to Buy It, and Where It Belongs in Aerospace and Defense
summary: 6061-T651 plate is a common structural aluminum for aerospace and defense hardware. Learn its thickness-dependent properties, specifications, applications, contract-origin checks, and buying requirements.
body_markdown:
### What is 6061-T651 plate used for in aerospace?


Structural brackets and mounts, machined avionics and optics housings, UAS airframe structure, ground support equipment, and tooling and inspection fixtures. It is chosen where weldability, corrosion resistance and machinability matter more than peak strength.


### What specification covers 6061-T651 plate?


ASTM B209 is common for commercial work and AMS 4027 is used on applicable aerospace plate; older drawings may reference AMS-QQ-A-250/11. Under ASTM B209, 6061-T651 plate minimums are 42,000 psi ultimate / 35,000 psi yield through 4 inches and 40,000 / 35,000 psi at 4.001–6 inches. Verify thicker stock and every aerospace order against the exact specification revision and mill certification.


### Is 6061-T651 good for defense parts?


For appropriate structure, housings, mounts, and ground-support equipment, yes. It is not an armor alloy; ballistic applications use other alloys to their own specifications. Follow the exact contract for origin and traceability: DFARS 252.225-7009 does not classify aluminum itself as a specialty metal, though other program clauses may require domestic origin or approved sources.


### Why is 6061-T651 better than T6 for machined parts?


T651 has been stress relieved by stretching after quenching. Machining unrelieved material unbalances trapped residual stress and the part moves, which shows up as bow or twist on large or thin-walled parts. T651 substantially reduces that stress at the mill, but it does not eliminate it.


### How thick does 6061-T651 plate come?


We stock 0.25 to 12 inches and cut to any rectangle on bandsaws with a 0.08 inch kerf. One square foot weighs 14.04 lbs per inch of thickness, so check the weight before ordering thick sections since it decides whether the order ships parcel or freight.
